quest.title: To Claim the Crown
quest.description: Time passes by. You're not sure if Aarav has completed his investigation behind the kidnapping case and uncovered the truth yet...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: A Parade of Providence: Act III
chapter.title: Gatherings and Partings

talks.objective: Learn about the situation from Aarav

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here. Sorry, I was just about to send someone to inform you. I only just finished interrogating the suspects.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What did you find out?

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Well... Lots of unexpected details, let's put it that way.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: The mercs themselves were surprisingly easy to catch. We just had someone dress up as Sachin, and they took the bait.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: But then it starts to get messy... During the interrogation, we learned that they were hired by Sachin's own child.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Why would someone wanna kidnap their own father? What's up with that?

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: It's anybody's guess at this point... In any event, apparently the guys we caught are just the tip of the iceberg. Most of them are still snooping around outside the city.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: We're diverting manpower as we speak to try and round them all up. Would you like to come along?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure. Let's go get to the bottom of all this.

talks.objective: Investigate the truth behind the kidnapping

dialogues.speaker: Levi
dialogues.text: Boss, we got more company...

dialogues.speaker: Mazaar
dialogues.text: Look, we were just doing what we were paid to do. You're punishing the wrong people here. You want the real culprit? It's this guy. He hired us to kidnap Sachin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened? Who beat you all up?

dialogues.speaker: Mazaar
dialogues.text: ...Wait, you mean you aren't with them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: With who? Who did this?

dialogues.speaker: Mazaar
dialogues.text: First there was this flying brat. Didn't bother asking any questions, just started throwing punches. After that, some guy wearing green came along and interrogated us for a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: I've got the confirmation I needed. This is the one who masterminded this whole plot — Jiwani, Sachin's son.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: If you have any questions for him, now's your chance to ask them. When you're done, I'm arresting them all and taking them back to the Akademiya for further interrogation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, why did you hire people to kidnap Sachin?

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: Hmph. Why do you think? Twenty years ago, he upped and left to go and live a carefree life, not giving a second thought for my welfare.

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: As if that's not bad enough already, he went and put his entire fortune in the care of the Akademiya, along with a contract saying that one day he'd pass it all on to a genius he admired.

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: That's my inheritance, by rights! You expect me to sit back and watch it go to someone else? If he won't give me what's mine, I'll just have to take it from him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Were you seriously planning to...

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: Of course! Didn't he say he would be here somewhere, watching the Championship from the shadows?

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: So I figured I get some people to nab him, then I make him change the contract. And if the Akademiya doesn't agree to hand over the goods, I make him publicly announce that I'm his chosen genius!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So did you find him?

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: No. The old fart knows how to stay hidden, I'll give him that. He's probably cooped up somewhere watching all this go on and laughing to himself.

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: I already thought he'd gone mad twenty years ago. And who knows what a madman is truly capable of...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you know about the Diadem of Knowledge?

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: Diadem of Knowledge? You mean that thing he donated to the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: Well, I can tell you that it's very expensive. He sold a lot of assets to purchase it back in the day.

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: Weird things started happening after he brought it home, too. For example, sometimes, we'd hear a high-pitched voice coming from the storage room.

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: Also, before donating it to the Akademiya, he once shut himself in that same store room and researched it non-stop for days.

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: Something was already seriously wrong with him by that point. Nothing he did shocked me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean, something wrong with him?

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: I only have a vague memory of it, since I was very young at the time. But I have the impression that he went out into the desert for research, and didn't return for many years.

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: When he finally did return, he was a changed person — he would mumble incomprehensibly and write essays day and night.

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: I asked if I could see what he'd written, but he chased me out of the room. Later, he went out somewhere and took his written essays with him. When he got back, he signed his contract with the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: ...Part of me wonders whether he'd already stopped being my father by that point. Perhaps the man we called "Sachin" was a demon from the desert who was wearing his skin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, you can stop now! You're creeping Paimon out!

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: You can believe me or not, doesn't matter to me — I've told you all I know. But if you do see Sachin, tell him this for me.

dialogues.speaker: Jiwani
dialogues.text: Whatever it is that he's researching out there, he'll always be garbage in my eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: You finished? In that case, come with us.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Well, we finally caught the guy behind all this. Thanks for providing us with the critical information.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Do you still have any lingering concerns?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The "Diadem of Knowledge"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Alhaitham's notes do mention that item...

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: ...Scribe Alhaitham looked into this matter?

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Hmm... Understood. Well, if you believe there to be an issue with the diadem, I'd suggest contacting the organizers and getting them to pause the competitions while we investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That makes sense! Okay then, let's get back to the venue! We need to tell Kareena what's going on!

talks.objective: Go to the main venue and find the staff member

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kareena!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Whew... You're finally back.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Where have you been? I looked everywhere for you... The third round's already started.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were out capturing some bad guys who wanted to kidnap Sachin...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But that's not important right now! We think there might be something wrong with the Diadem of Knowledge, and we'd like to investigate it!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: The Diadem? That seems unlikely.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: The Diadem of Knowledge has been used in every Extravaganza over the last two decades, always without incident... Why has this come up now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Some new information has come to light.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Hmm. This is pretty serious. Let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Okay, here's the situation: The diadem is currently in Mawtiyima Forest. We moved it there before the third round began.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: In the third round, contestants have to go into Mawtiyima Forest, find the diadem, bring it back, and place it on the stand. The first person to do this gets 4 points.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Considering how close the scores are between our contestants, whoever wins this round is very likely to be the winner of the whole competition.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: As such, I suspect competition to be very fierce. You might not make it in time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We have to give it a shot.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: I'll mark the diadem's location for you. Please head there immediately. Let's hope nothing happens...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright. Let's go!

talks.objective: Return to the finish line and observe the situation

dialogues.text: At long last... Someone to inherit my estate... and with it, my research.
Come, Kaveh. Come to me, my child...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...How do you know my name? Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: I am Sachin. Well, to be precise, I am but a fragment of Sachin's mind.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: Fate is a curious thing... Seeing you reminds me of another I once met. But you are made of sterner stuff than he, more cognizant of the trials and tribulations of this world. It is you who are worthy to inherit all that I once owned.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: We meet for the first time, children. But what I mean to say now is of utmost importance. So please, pay attention and bear witness.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: You have all performed outstandingly in this Interdarshan Championship. The Akademiya has many rare talents among its ranks, and you are the creme of the creme.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: But if I were to choose a successor, I would choose you, Kaveh. Not only because you were victorious, but also due to our similarities in character.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Me? Similar to you?

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: Why, yes. Both of us have the misfortune to be idealists — and that is the source of our misery.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: Twenty-eight years ago, I came to the desert and lived there for eight full years. What do you think I saw there? Alas, endless strife and slaughter...

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: Conflict over water sources, robbing of merchant caravans, exploitation of the people... relentlessly, day after day. Beyond the Wall of Samiel lay a completely different world from the one I knew.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: The things I witnessed there tormented me greatly. I wished desperately to find a way to save them.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...So? Did you find a way?

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: As a Vahumana scholar, I tried to use Vahumana knowledge to find the answer.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: I researched history and anthropology, performed countless experiments on human nature, and even sought out the scholars living deep in the desert who call themselves the "Lost Darshan"...

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: But in the end, I found that the answer I sought simply did not exist.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: It was not possible to simply assign blame for these transgressions to any one party, for the sins are carved into humanity's very nature. Our nature begets conflict, and conflict begets destruction. This is the inexorable truth.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: The aim of my research was to draw lessons from history, but what I discovered was that history offers no such guidance... Things can only ever go from bad to worse!

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: After this realization, I could no longer see the meaning in anything that I had ever learned. Consumed by an overwhelming sense of emptiness, I could no longer bear to face life... and so I decided to bring my life to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: But before I went through with it, a strange twist of fate led me to come into the possession of this diadem, which has the ability to preserve part of one's consciousness. Into it, I placed my experiences, before requesting that the Akademiya manage my estate.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: As I thought, the contract you signed with the Akademiya was, in essence, your will.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: But if you'd given up hope on this world, why did you feel the need to do this?

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: I mentioned that I had performed a great many experiments concerning human nature... You may regard this as the very last experiment of them all.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: The Akademiya has no shortage of genius talents, nurturing the brightest minds of every generation. And so, with a handsome reward to draw out the worthiest of individuals, my hope was that one day, I would find one who could untangle the mystery of human nature once and for all, and help to move the world onto a better path.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I see, so you desired a successor who was not only a genius, but who also understood the suffering of ordinary people. Such a person would have a clearer understanding of humanity, society, and the world.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: But did you ever consider that wealth numbs the human heart to the pain in the world? Even an idealist may be incapable of following through on your wishes after inheriting your wealth.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: You are highly intelligent... Yet you are not the sort of person who would understand my line of thinking. To me, this is also part of the experiment — part of my investigation into human nature.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: Whether my successor suffers as a consequence of my research or succumbs to an indulgence in pleasure-seeking, my research will have progressed.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: I grieve the fundamental sickness of the world, I regret the unbearable weight of its history, and I lament the research that I failed to complete.

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: And this, Kaveh, my dear child... is why you will be of great utility to me.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You're... you're absolutely certain that you want to give me everything you owned, for me to do with as I please?

dialogues.speaker: Sachin
dialogues.text: I have faith in what I see in you. Now, wear the diadem, Kaveh, and complete the journey that I could not.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I guess that'll be the end of that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kaveh...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Are you alright? Any physical discomfort?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'm... fine... Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Thanks, Tighnari. Don't worry about me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Don't push yourself too hard.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Kaveh...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Kaveh may have broken the diadem, but he successfully completed the task prior to that.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: According to the rules, this makes him the victor of round three. Points-wise, this also makes him the winner of the Interdarshan Championship.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: As the champion, and Sachin's personally designated successor, Kaveh has obtained the rights to inherit the entirety of his estate.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: For the avoidance of doubt, can you confirm that it is your intention to donate all of Sachin's wealth?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Like I said... he thought that the world is a bad place. Well then, let's use what he left behind to change it for the better.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Rejecting the world will achieve nothing. He and I... We're not the same.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Alright. As the scribe, I will make a record of this incident on file.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The sages will contact you in person for details on how exactly Sachin's estate is to be used.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...That sounds fine.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I don't know if his research findings were right, nor would I know how to finish his research for him.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: But what I do know is that by ending this here, no contestants will have to suffer.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: We won't be the last. There will be more championships to come... and countless future scholars will follow in our footsteps.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Sachin's words can only cause pain. But... not anymore. No one else has to hear them now.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: We're all scholars here. I know full well that shutting down his views like this is autocratic and arrogant... Fine by me. I'll bear that responsibility.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's the least I can do. And, well... it's the only thing I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well said. What you've expressed is a sense of justice and idealism that many aspire to, but few dare follow through with.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I say this despite the fact that, in my view, it's quite ridiculous. You have long been aware of what your flaws are, but your pride alone prevents you from admitting it.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, your perspective is well-suited to appearing in a victory speech. Contestant Kaveh, on behalf of the organizing committee, it is my honor to congratulate you on your victory.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What? Please. I don't need your insincere praise.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Anyway, this isn't the time or place for debates. Keep your commentary focused on the competition, not my views.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Congratulations, Kaveh! Also, you'll need to prepare for the award ceremony...

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Why this year...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alhaitham, Nilou, have you seen any of the other contestants?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: No. No one's completed the task yet... Why, has something happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There might be a problem with the diadem... Oh, but Alhaitham, you must know something about it, right?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Whatever do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You...! Forget it! We'll go find it first. We'll ask you again later!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aarav, are you sure this is the right place? Something feels off...

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: I'm positive. But I don't understand why they're all unconscious on the ground...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's weird... The locator's stopped working. Is the forest interfering with it? Ugh, let's just go grab the diadem!
